title: Which fraction word is the smallest, and which the biggest?
description: Six fraction words are sorted by how many whole units each one holds, then by how many fourths and halves, to arrange them from smallest to biggest.
teaching_notes: One idea: sort fractions by the whole number first, then by the part left over. Watch for students who think one and a quarter is smaller than three quarters because the quarter looks small.

source: Arrange these fraction words in order of size from the smallest to the biggest in the empty box below: One and a half, three quarters, one and a quarter, half, quarter, two and a half.
video_script.why: The child writes each fraction word as a number, sorts by whole units and then by parts of one whole, and arranges the six from smallest to biggest.
video_script.substitution: Write quarter as 1/4, half as 1/2 and three quarters as 3/4, then sort the six by how many wholes each one holds.
video_script.anchor: Six fraction words in a mixed-up order, to arrange from smallest to biggest
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest is a quarter and the biggest is two and a half

final_answer.spoken: quarter, half, three quarters, one and a quarter, one and a half, two and a half

video_script.fraction_reading: one fourth, one half, three fourths, one and one fourth, one and one half, two and one half
never_show: the six fractions in their sorted order before the answer beat
maths_rules: quarter = 1/4, half = 1/2, three quarters = 3/4, one and a quarter = 1 1/4, one and a half = 1 1/2, two and a half = 2 1/2
less than 1 whole: 1/4, 1/2, 3/4; 1/2 = 2/4, so in fourths they are 1, 2 and 3 fourths
between 1 and 2: 1 1/4 and 1 1/2, and the fourth is smaller than the half
video_script.design: One idea: sort by wholes first, then by the part. Assumes the child knows half and quarter on a bar. The six cards stay on the board to the end.
